results.primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: a May 2026 report described Capesize rates reaching a two-year high on stronger demand and tightening vessel supply, while August 2026 BIMCO-related reporting warned that apparent 2026 strength was substantially driven by forced rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut. The exact current BDI/Capesize/Panamax commodity-volume cycle is therefore not sufficiently time-consistent.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk shipping rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening ship supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial because of forced rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry Bulk Shipping Faces 2027 Supply Glut: BIMCO Warns Hormuz Rerouting Boost Will Reverse

results.primary_cause: Searches found evidence of continuing storage and memory demand growth, but not sufficiently specific, time-consistent evidence confirming a NAND pricing, SSD/controller/module inventory, and demand cycle. Available evidence does not establish the exact nominated cycle or resolve contradictory cycle-direction implications.

supporting_evidence.claim: The 2026 Future of Memory and Storage Conference highlighted continued growth in storage and memory demand driven by AI and data growth.
supporting_evidence.source_title: 2026 FMS Shows Storage And Memory Market Continued Growth

counter_evidence.claim: The available search evidence discusses structural NAND demand and supply dynamics but does not verify the current exact NAND pricing, inventory, and module/controller cycle required for activation.
counter_evidence.source_title: The Next NAND Decade: Why Supply Can’t Catch Demand The Way It Used To
